config.title: mask and clip-path

intro.title: mask and clip-path
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a visually engaging webpage that uses CSS to reveal and hide parts of images in creative shapes. You will learn the core concepts of masking and clipping, which control the visible area of an element. The main technologies involved are the CSS properties `mask` and `clip-path`. As a beginner, you'll start with simple shapes and progress to more complex effects, all within a single CSS file. By the end, you'll be able to apply these properties to design unique visual compositions without altering the original image files.
intro.usecase: The mask and clip-path properties are essential for creating sophisticated visual effects in modern web interfaces. Developers use these techniques to create non-rectangular UI elements like circular profile images, custom-shaped buttons, and decorative image cutouts in dashboards and marketing sites. In e-commerce platforms, clip-path helps create visually appealing product image galleries with unique shapes, while masks are used for subtle image transitions and overlays in hero sections. These CSS properties allow designers to break away from traditional rectangular layouts, enabling more creative and engaging user experiences across applications.

objectives: Implement a CSS mask using a gradient to create a fading transparency effect on an image.
Apply the clip-path property with basic shapes to crop elements into circles and polygons.
Construct a visual composition by layering masked and clipped elements to achieve complex designs.
Configure mask properties such as mask-size and mask-position to control the masking area.
Update clip-path coordinates dynamically to create interactive shape transformations.
Integrate mask and clip-path techniques to enhance UI components like cards or avatars.

steps.title: Apply clip-path with inset() function
steps.instruction: Add a clip-path rule using the inset() function to create a rectangular cutout on the third box element.
steps.hint: The inset() function creates an inner rectangle by specifying distances from the element's edges. Use clip-path: inset(20px); to create a 20px inset from all sides.
steps.expectedOutcome: The third box element will have a rectangular cutout effect with 20px inset from all edges.
successCriteria: The third box element has a clip-path property with inset(20px) applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct syntax: clip-path: inset(20px);
steps.feedbackWrong: The clip-path rule for the third box element is missing or incorrect. Try using inset(20px) to create the rectangular cutout.

steps.instruction: Add a mask property with radial-gradient() to the second box element to create a circular transparency pattern.
steps.hint: Use mask: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 50%, black 50%); to create a circular mask that makes the center transparent.
steps.expectedOutcome: The second box element will have a circular transparency mask applied, creating a see-through circular area in the center.
successCriteria: The second box element has a mask property with radial-gradient() that creates circular transparency.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the mask property with radial-gradient() on the second box element.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Try adding mask: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 50%, black 50%); to the second box element.
